text:
incident-bot: PAGER: P1 — High GPU capacity degradation detected in us-west-2. Autoscaler queue length > 10k, pool 'gpu-prod-usw2' exhausted. Linking dashboard: https://internal.redwood/inz/graphs/abc123 :rotating_light:
michelle (oncall): On it. Seeing a spike in queued requests and ~30% error rate on hosted API. Are we getting Xid/ooms?
sanjay: yes: worker logs show repeated CUDA Xid 31 and kernel OOM entries on a subset of nodes. Example from gpu-node-17:
```
[GPU] Xid (PCIe) 31: Ecc error: GPU hung
[Kernel] OutOfMemory: kill process 2345 (driver-daemon) total-vm:xxxkB
```
michelle (oncall): ack. Any autoscaler errors?
infra-bot: Autoscaler alert: scale_attempt_failed: allocation_error (insufficient_resource) at 2991234580, last_scale_time 2991234500. Pool quota remaining: 0/8 (burst exhausted).
ops-lead: If quota is zero we might need manual intervention. What blocked allocations? scheduling or driver registration?
sanjay: Scheduling & registration both. New nodes boot but driver fails to register repeatedly — likely driver crash loop due to the Xid/OOM. We have ~4 nodes in flapping state: gpu-node-{17,18,21,24}.
michelle (oncall): Rolling mitigation suggestions:
- cordon affected nodes
- restart driver daemon on candidate spare nodes
- temporarily raise autoscaler hard limit to allow manual scale if quota can be reclaimed
- fallback traffic to cpu-backend for non-SLA requests
- apply a constrained routing rule to limit bursty load to dedicated pool
Which of these we can do now?
support-eng: We can implement CPU fallback in ~5m, but that will increase latency for customers on those requests. We should classify which customers to move. customer-success: I can identify affected customers from the 503s: three enterprise tenants showing increased error rates (ent-alpha, ent-beta, sandbox-gamma). ent-alpha is producing high business impact.
ops-lead: michelle, approve cordon + driver restart and manual scale to bridge. I'll own quota reclamation with cloud.
michelle (oncall): Doing cordon on gpu-node-17 and 18 now:
```
kubectl cordon gpu-node-17
kubectl cordon gpu-node-18
```
michelle (oncall): Restarting driver daemon on gpu-node-21 via runbook step 2:
```
ssh ops@gpu-node-21 'sudo systemctl restart nvidia-driver-daemon'
```
sanjay: Logs after restart show driver coming up then Xid 31 again after ~45s. Hypothesis: some workload pattern triggers kernel-level OOM under current driver build.
ops-lead: We should pull those nodes out of rotation until we get the driver stable. Manual scale up attempted but hit quota. Initiating emergency quota request to cloud: ticket CLQ-789 initiated. ETA ~12m.
infra-bot: Manual scale command blocked: allocation rejected: "driver_registration_timeout" for nodes boot-045, boot-046.
michelle (oncall): While cloud works quota, let's reduce token consumption by routing high-cost models to smaller variants. Applying routing policy override for model:redwood-vlarge -> redwood-large for hosted tier.
```
curl -X POST https://internal.redwood/api/routing/override -d '{"model":"redwood-vlarge","fallback":"redwood-large","ttl":600}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer ***'
```
support-eng: Applied fallback rule, metrics show per-request tokens down ~35% on the next window. Queue growth slowed but still above threshold.
customer-success: Ent-alpha notified. They've acknowledged and asked for ETA; I told them we're doing mitigations and will update in 30m.
ops-lead: quota ticket triaged to high; cloud flagged a stale reservation that can be freed. If freed, we can scale +6 GPUs. Proceeding to reclaim.
michelle (oncall): Next I want to drain one healthy spare node and run stress test to try to reproduce. Also create a temporary autoscaler override to ignore 'driver_registration_timeout' while we stabilize nodes (with manual monitoring).
leah (oncall-next): I'll take the handoff at +30m. Please leave a summary and list of open actions before rotation.
michelle (oncall): Summary so far:
- Impact: elevated 5xx rates and increased latency for hosted API in us-west-2; three customers affected (ent-alpha highest).
- Cause: driver/runtime instability (CUDA Xid 31, OOM) on a subset of GPU nodes causing effective capacity loss; autoscaler attempts blocked due to exhausted quota and driver registration timeouts.
- Mitigations applied: cordoned flapping nodes, restarted driver on 21, routing fallback to smaller model, partial CPU fallback configured for low-priority traffic, emergency cloud quota ticket (CLQ-789) opened, manual scale pending reclaim.
- Open actions: 1) reclaim quota (ops-lead), 2) reproduce and collect driver crash dumps (sanjay), 3) extend routing fallback TTL and prepare rollback (support-eng), 4) notify/coordinate with driver vendor/engineering (michelle & sanjay), 5) handoff to leah in 30m.
ops-lead: Quota reclaimed, cloud freed 6 GPUs. Initiating manual scale now:
```
kubectl -n infra scale deployment gpu-autoscaler --replicas=5
```
infra-bot: Manual scale succeeded. 4 new nodes booting. Registration progress: 2/4 registered, 1/4 delayed.
sanjay: Captured driver logs and core on gpu-node-17 for analysis and uploaded to /artifacts/incident-2991234567/; initial trace indicates a memory leak in driver under sustained KV cache growth.
michelle (oncall): Good. Once new nodes stabilize we'll uncordon spare capacity and reroute traffic back. Estimated full recovery in 18m.
customer-success: ent-alpha replied: "Thanks for quick action. Please keep us posted; we'll pause heavy batch jobs for next hour."
leah (oncall-next): I'll be on deck. michelle, leave the exact next steps and link to the artifact.
michelle (oncall): Leaving notes in the incident ticket INC-2991 and artifact link above. Handoff: monitor registration progress, confirm error rate drops below 1%, keep routing fallback active until postmortem determines fix.
incident-bot: Incident status updated to 'mitigated' at 2991234620 (partial mitigation). Postmortem required.
michelle (oncall): closing handoff. leah, take it from here. :white_check_mark:
